About Role We are seeking a hands-on Cloud Security Engineer to help secure the infrastructure and platforms that power our global Fin-Tech systems. You will collaborate closely with platform engineers, DevOps teams, and application developers to proactively identify risks, automate security controls, and improve the overall security posture of our systems. This role requires someone who can think like an attacker but build like an engineer. You are someone who enjoys identifying weaknesses, designing preventative controls, and building security automation that scales with the platform. You will work closely with our engineering teams across India, the United States, Nigeria, and Kenya, collaborating across time zones to help build and secure a world-class Fin-Tech platform serving millions of users globally. As a company, we are passionate about our customers, fearless in the face of barriers, and driven by data. As an engineering team, we value bottom-up innovation and decentralized decision-making. We believe the best ideas can come from anyone in the company. We work hard to create an environment where everyone feels empowered to propose solutions, challenge assumptions, and drive meaningful impact. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a fast-moving, innovative, and customer-focused setting and want to contribute to building scalable, reliable, and efficient backend systems. As a company, we are passionate about our customers, fearless in the face of barriers, and driven by data. Responsibilities Identify and secure attack surfaces across our AWS infrastructure, Kubernetes clusters, and internal platforms by proactively assessing misconfigurations, access risks, and exposed services. Design and implement preventative cloud security guardrails including IAM hardening, network controls, secrets management, and infrastructure security best practices. Conduct security design reviews for new services and infrastructure changes to identify architectural risks before systems reach production. Build and integrate security checks directly into CI/CD pipelines to enforce automated scanning for vulnerabilities, container images, infrastructure configurations, and application dependencies. Develop automation and internal tooling to detect, prevent, and remediate security issues such as leaked secrets, excessive permissions, insecure configurations, and vulnerable dependencies. Perform threat modeling and adversarial analysis of infrastructure and application systems to identify realistic attack paths and improve system defenses. Improve visibility into the security posture of our systems through monitoring, logging, and security signal generation across cloud infrastructure and workloads. Investigate security incidents and vulnerabilities, perform root cause analysis, and implement long-term fixes to prevent recurrence. Collaborate closely with platform, infrastructure, and application engineering teams to ensure security is embedded in development workflows and infrastructure design. Contribute to building scalable security practices including vulnerability management processes, security automation frameworks, and infrastructure security standards. Qualifications 4+ years of experience in cloud security, DevSecOps, security engineering, or related roles involving infrastructure and application security. Strong understanding of applied cryptography and ability to choose the right security tools, techniques, and approach for securing systems from a variety of threats. Strong hands-on experience securing AWS environments including IAM policies, networking controls, access management, logging, and infrastructure hardening. Practical experience working with Kubernetes and containerized environments, including securing container images, workloads, and cluster configurations. Experience integrating security controls into CI/CD pipelines and development workflows, including automated vulnerability scanning and dependency security checks. Ability to write automation and security tooling using scripting or programming languages such as Python, Go, or similar. Familiarity with Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Terraform and an understanding of securing infrastructure configurations and deployment pipelines. Experience identifying and remediating cloud security risks such as excessive IAM permissions, exposed services, insecure secrets management, and vulnerable infrastructure components. Understanding of common cloud and application security threats including privilege escalation, credential leakage, network exposure, and supply chain vulnerabilities. Strong problem-solving mindset with the ability to think adversarially about systems and proactively identify potential attack paths. Excellent collaboration and communication skills (verbal as well as written) with the ability to work closely with engineering teams and other stakeholders to improve security posture without slowing development velocity. Bonus experience includes security research, penetration testing, bug bounty participation, building internal security tooling, or contributions to security-focused open-source projects. Bonus abilities include ability to lead and mentor a team, and ability to drive complex projects spanning code bases, systems, and people. Through Maven Enterprise, the company partners with more than 2,300 employers and health plans to provide end-to-end women's and family health programs spanning fertility and family building, maternity and newborn care, parenting and pediatrics, and menopause and midlife — improving clinical outcomes, reducing healthcare costs, and expanding equitable access to high-quality care at scale. Recognized for innovation and industry leadership, Maven has been named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, and FORTUNE Best Places to Work. Learn more at mavenclinic.com

An award-winning culture working towards an important mission –  Maven Clinic is a recipient of over 30 workplace and innovation awards, including: 

• TIME 100 Most Influential Companies (2023, 2026)

• Fortune Change the World (2024)

• CNBC Disruptor 50 List (2022, 2023, 2024)

• Fortune Best Workplaces for Millennials (2024)

• Fortune Best Workplaces in Health Care (2024)

• Fast Company Most Innovative Companies (2020, 2023)

• Fortune Best Workplaces NY (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

About the Role:

Maven is looking for a Head of Member Growth to own one of the most important numbers in the company: enrollments. This role is directly accountable for driving member enrollment into Maven's programs across our core business — and, by extension, the revenue those enrollments generate. You will own the enrollment engine end to end, from awareness through activation, turning eligible lives into engaged members.

Enrollment is not a single-team problem. It sits at the intersection of nearly every function at Maven, and this role is built for someone who thrives there. You'll partner daily with Client Success (who own the client relationships that unlock eligible populations), Marketing (member acquisition and lifecycle), Product (enrollment experience and funnel), Finance (targets, forecasting, and unit economics), Data (measurement, segmentation, and attribution), and Clinical and Operations teams. Because so many teams touch enrollment, a core part of the job is holding those cross-functional partners accountable to their piece of the machine — the engine only works when every team delivers its part.

This is a player-coach role. You will lead a small, high-caliber team while remaining deeply hands-on yourself every day. Although it carries a Senior Director title, it is explicitly NOT a leaned-out management position for someone who wants to direct a team from a distance. This is a hard requirement: the person in this seat reads the data themselves, pressure-tests the funnel, drafts the plan, and does the work alongside the team. We are looking for a builder and operator who also develops people — not a manager who has stepped away from the work.

We're also looking for someone who can expand the definition of the job. A great deal of enrollment optimization work is already underway, but there is not enough strategic thinking about fundamentally new ways to drive enrollments — approaches that don't simply depend on securing permission to communicate with a client's employees. This role is expected to find and open those new avenues, not just optimize the existing ones.

What You'll Do:

• Own member growth for the Core Business: Be directly accountable for enrollment targets across Maven's core business and for the revenue those enrollments drive. Set the strategy, build the plan, and act as a control tower across all cross-functional teams driving revenue to deliver the results quarter over quarter.

• Build and run a scalable enrollment engine: Own the full journey from eligible population to enrolled, activated member — spanning client launches, member acquisition and messaging, the enrollment product experience, and re-engagement of eligible-but-not-enrolled members.

• Expand the playbook and deliver new strategies to drive sustainable member growth: Think strategically and from first principles about new ways to grow enrollments beyond today's optimization work — including partnerships and approaches that don't rely solely on permission to communicate with a client's employees. Identify, size, and open avenues that expand the team's purview and unlock new growth. 

• Optimize relentlessly around data: Build and consistently iterate on the funnel, and create systems that enable quick diagnoses of opportunities. Build operational metrics that act as leading KPIs for each team contributing to enrollments and bring quantitative rigor into how teams execute against targets.

• Hold the cross-functional machine accountable: Partner daily with Client Success, Marketing, Product, Finance, Data, Clinical, Payer, Sales, and Operations — and hold each team accountable to its operational KPIs in the enrollment process. Serve as the connective tissue that keeps every part of the engine delivering.

• Operate as a player-coach: Lead and develop a small, high-performing team while staying in the execution and details. Set the bar for rigor and hands-on execution by doing the work, coaching through it, and multiplying the team's impact rather than stepping back from it. This is a role that comes with an expectation that you directly execute on the work.

• Instrument and forecast: Partner with Data and Finance to build the measurement, segmentation, attribution, and forecasting needed to know exactly what is and isn't working, and to forecast enrollment and revenue with confidence.

What You'll Bring:

• 10+ years of experience driving growth, enrollment, acquisition, or revenue outcomes, with a track record of personally owning and hitting a number — ideally in healthcare, benefits, marketplaces, consumer subscription, or another environment with a complex funnel and multiple stakeholders.

• A hands-on player-coach. You are energized by being in the details daily — the data, the funnel, the plan, the execution — and you lead a small team as a way to multiply your own hands-on impact, not to step back from the work. This is a hard requirement for the role. 

• Elite quantitative ability as a core competency. You can build and interrogate a funnel model yourself, size opportunities, design experiments, and instinctively optimize around data rather than intuition. Strong quant is non-negotiable.

• Strategic range. Beyond optimizing what exists, you can spot and pursue fundamentally new approaches to enrollment that expand the team's purview — not just incremental improvements to current channels.

• Cross-functional leadership and accountability. Proven ability to align and mobilize many teams — Client Success, Marketing, Product, Finance, Data, Clinical, Operations — around a shared goal without direct authority over most of them, and to hold each accountable to its operational commitments.

• Commercial instincts. You understand how enrollment translates into revenue and unit economics, and you can partner with Finance on targets and forecasting.

• Comfort in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment with high visibility and direct accountability for a top-line company metric.

The base salary range for this role is $204,000.00 - $270,000.00 per year. You will also be entitled to receive bonus, equity, and benefits. Individual pay decisions are based on qualifications, experience, and skillset.

We are seeking a strategic and analytical Chief of Staff to partner with our Chief Customer Officer (CCO) in driving business performance across our Customer organization. This role combines financial and operational strategy, data-driven decision-making, and cross-functional collaboration to improve customer retention, revenue performance, and organizational effectiveness.

The ideal candidate brings strong financial and business acumen, a collaborative mindset, and the ability to translate complex information into actionable insights that inform executive decisions and strengthen financial and operational accountability.

What You'll Do

• Customer revenue metrics: In partnership with Finance, which owns ARR and financial reporting, to ensure customer metrics (ARR movement, gross and net revenue retention, renewal rates on up for renewal revenue, cohort views and churn drivers) follow Thoma Bravo standards and best-in-class methods. Translates those metrics into the customer organization's view, measures renewal forecast accuracy, and reports on cross-sell and upsell pipeline, which Renewals and Sales own.

• Executive and board narrative: Prepares the CCO's materials for the executive leadership team, board, Thoma Bravo operating reviews and QBRs, framing performance, risk and investment asks in terms of business outcomes. Ensures what the board sees reconciles to how the organization operates.

• Renewal and retention reporting: Owns renewal rate reporting and variance analysis of the official forecast against plan and actuals, explaining the drivers behind the numbers.

• Renewal and retention plan and resource models: In partnership with Finance, builds the customer organization's annual renewal and retention plan (historical baselines, renewal rate assumptions and targets) and the headcount, coverage-ratio and capacity models tied to book-of-business segmentation.

• Customer health and signals: Delivers the customer health scoring model and churn and risk analysis.

• Customer reporting requirements and CCO analysis: Sets the customer organization's reporting requirements across Salesforce, the data warehouse and BI tools, aligned with Finance's metric definitions, which Systems & Operations and Data & Analytics build to. Handles the CCO's own analysis and reporting requests.

• Cross-functional Alignment: Works with Revenue Operations and CRO leadership team to align on strategies and reporting for improving Net Retention Rate. Works with the Product Strategy team to align on churn analysis and forecasting by product.

What You'll Bring

• Significant experience in strategic finance, FP&A, business operations, revenue operations, customer success operations, or a related field, ideally within a B2B SaaS environment.

• Strong understanding of SaaS business models and recurring revenue metrics, including ARR, GRR, NRR, renewals, and churn.

• Experience translating business needs into reporting and analytics requirements, with familiarity using tools such as Salesforce, Excel, SQL, Power BI, or Tableau.

• Ability to analyze complex datasets and communicate insights clearly to executive audiences.

• Familiarity with CRM, reporting, and business intelligence tools such as Salesforce, Excel, SQL, Power BI, or Tableau.

• Strong collaboration, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to influence across teams.

• Experience in private equity-backed environments or supporting executive and board-level reporting is a plus.

Associate Product Manager

Location: Bangalore
Role Type: Full-time

This role is for someone who wants to get their hands dirty, move fast, and solve real problems in a space that matters. It will be a grind. If you're looking for a large team with clearly defined swim lanes, this isn't it. If you want to own things end-to-end from day one, read on.

What you'll be doing
You'll work across two of our core products: Lumen (our energy management platform) and Contracts (how we structure, price, and operationalise renewable energy agreements for C&I businesses).
• Lumen: Work with engineering and design to ship features — bill digitisation, multi-site dashboards, contract monitoring, Scope 2 reporting. Understand what our customers need, write clear specs, and follow through to delivery.
• Contracts: Help translate complex energy contract logic into usable product flows. Think through how a CFO or facility manager experiences a contract — from onboarding to monthly settlement — and make it smoother.
• Customer Feedback Loops: Talk to customers. Sit in on calls. Synthesise what you hear into things the team can act on.
• Data & Analytics: Dig into usage data, identify patterns, and flag things that matter. We have a large and growing dataset of electricity bills and metering data — there's a lot to find.
• Cross-functional Work: Work closely with our energy, sales, and engineering teams. At this stage, product sits at the centre of almost everything.

What we're looking for
Qualifications
• Recently completed a bachelors programme at a Tier I institution (IITs, IIMs, BITS, NIT-K).
• At least one prior product internship — we want to see that you've written a PRD, talked to users, or shipped something, even if small.
• Strong written communication. You'll be writing specs, summarising customer calls, and flagging issues clearly.
• Comfortable with ambiguity. Early-stage means the brief changes. You need to be okay with that.
• Genuine curiosity about energy. You don't need to know what a DISCOM is on day one — but you should find it interesting when you find out.

The kind of person we want
We want someone who thinks energy is a genuinely interesting problem, who reads things they don't have to read, and who'll push back when something doesn't make sense.
Early-stage startups are hard. The upside is that you'll do more in six months here than you might in two years elsewhere.

ca2527f2534922f8.description:
Who We Are
Heritage is building the Modern Investment Office, supporting some of the most prominent families globally to achieve their capital enhancement and preservation goals.
Our vision is to help clients build enduring wealth across generations by combining institutional-grade investment sourcing with personalized portfolio construction, cutting-edge technology, and deep sector expertise. We aim to make sophisticated private market opportunities and modern wealth solutions more transparent, connected, and actionable.
Our team comprises a diverse international group of individuals from leading organizations and with diverse backgrounds, including private equity, venture capital, banking, software development, law, and entrepreneurship. We are committed to attracting top-notch talent and providing opportunities for growth and development based on their individual strengths and interests.
Your Role
Your role as Portfolio Manager is part of our Portfolio Management team. The mission of the role is to ensure that the portfolios of our UHNW clients are actively monitored, well-constructed and aligned with their objectives. 
The Associate is allocated to a defined group of European client relationships, covering OCIO and portfolio advisory mandates. Portfolios are multi-asset, spanning liquid and semi-liquid investments, often across multiple banks and counterparties. The role carries direct ownership of portfolio oversight, from asset allocation, fees, liquidity and risk to the quality of the investments proposed to clients.
The role reports to Head of Portfolio Management, and cross-reports to the Relationship Managers. It works in close collaboration with both, providing RMs with timely, high-quality investment input and the confidence that their clients are being taken care of even when they are not looking.
Key Responsibilities
• Oversee client portfolios for OCIO and portfolio advisory clients, playing an active role in shaping clients’ portfolios across a range of asset classes (fixed income, public equity, alternative assets...)
• Maintain clear visibility on asset allocation, fees, liquidity and risk across client portfolios
• Monitor performance, attribution and risk metrics, identifying portfolio drift, concentration risks and misalignment with client objectives
• Assess investments and opportunities proposed by banks and other counterparties (funds, structured products, discretionary mandates, alternatives), forming clear and well-reasoned views
• Identify sub-optimal products (fees, quality, overlap) and propose better alternatives
• Support Relationship Managers with timely, high-quality investment input ahead of and following client discussions
• Track transactions, changes and next steps, so that monitoring and follow-up actions are not missed
• Support business development meetings with prospective clients
• Work closely with the Portfolio Management team on portfolio construction and investment decisions, with a view to contributing to the continuous improvement of our investment process
What We Are Looking For
• Outstanding academic background with a master's degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering or related disciplines
• Solid experience in portfolio management or advisory, ideally for UHNW individuals, within a Multi-Family Office, OCIO, Private Bank or Wealth Manager
• Strong grasp of portfolio construction and asset allocation, including strategic vs tactical allocation and diversification principles, and the ability to assess multi-asset portfolios (liquid and semi-liquid)
• Ability to analyze investment products proposed by banks and asset managers, with a solid understanding of fees (explicit and implicit), liquidity terms and risk drivers
• Experience monitoring portfolio performance, attribution and risk metrics
• Comfortable interacting with sophisticated UHNW clients and Relationship Managers, and able to explain investment concepts clearly and credibly, both verbally and in writing
• Strong attention to detail in portfolio reviews, transaction monitoring and documentation, and ability to work in a structured, process-driven environment
• Experience in manager selection or due diligence is a plus
• Basic financial modelling and portfolio analytics skills are a plus
• International exposure or experience working with non-Italian institutions is a plus
• Tech-savvy, with experience in a portfolio analytics or wealth reporting platform (Addepar is a plus)
• Effective communicator with a collaborative and multicultural mindset
• Highly motivated and proactive, with a hands-on and flexible attitude
• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic and fast-growing environment
• Fluent in English. Other languages constitute a plus
Location: Remote work is fine, but being based at a Heritage office is a plus.
What We Offer
• 
An exceptional team and environment: You will work alongside highly talented professionals from leading global institutions such as Carlyle, CD&R, McKinsey, Bain, Goldman Sachs, and top technology companies. We operate with a high talent bar, intellectual rigor, and a strong focus on excellence.
• 
High ownership and client-facing scope: You will take ownership of the oversight of UHNW client portfolios, working closely with senior stakeholders, Relationship Managers and clients. You will have significant responsibility in assessing investment opportunities and shaping the quality of the portfolios we manage and advise on.
• 
Exposure to the intersection of wealth management and technology: You will work on complex multi-asset portfolios and sophisticated wealth structures, using Heritage's proprietary platform to consolidate and analyze portfolio data, and contribute to the continuous evolution of a technology-driven wealth management offering.
• 
International scope and strong culture: You will operate in a diverse, international team representing 15+ nationalities, with hiring across multiple geographies. We foster a collaborative and ambitious culture, supported by regular team offsites and opportunities to build strong relationships.

At Heritage, we are proud to have a diverse team representing over 15 nationalities, with all communication conducted in English. We are deeply committed to providing equal opportunities and work actively to remove potential biases in our hiring process by involving a Hiring Committee in all decision-making.

Commercial Data Scientist

Doximity is the leading clinical AI company with the largest network of U.S. clinicians. Doximity’s AI-powered workflow platform is trusted by over 85% of U.S. physicians and 300+ health systems. Doximity's mission is to help clinicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients. 

At Doximity, we value curiosity, ownership, inclusion, and a commitment to making a meaningful impact. If you're excited about solving complex problems that improve healthcare, we'd love to hear from you.

This role can be filled in the Northeast (New York, NJ, Philadelphia, Boston), our San Francisco headquarters, OR other remote locations in the U.S.

As a Commercial Data Scientist, you’ll work within cross-functional delivery teams alongside other analysts, engineers, and commercial stakeholders in discovering data insights to help improve healthcare.

How you’ll make an impact:

• Deliver novel and impactful insights for client organizations using machine learning and AI technologies.

• Work closely with our Product, Platform Data, Insights & Strategy, and Sales teams to create client-facing analyses.

• Showcase your engineering skills by creating data products from scratch and automating code so they can be re-used by other teammates and future projects.

• Leverage Doximity's extensive datasets to identify and classify behavioral patterns of medical professionals on our platform.

• Embrace the challenge of a fast-paced environment to exceed client expectations

The Core Values of the Client Intelligence team

As an organization we value diversity - in backgrounds and in experiences. Healthcare is a universal concern, and we need people from all backgrounds to help build a better future for all. Below are additional core values specific to the Insights Team.

• Collaboration—The best candidates and teammates are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.

• Passion for Data—You’re going to help our clients and team members with data-driven decision making. We need someone that can manipulate millions of rows of data and also ask the right questions to find the important insights.

• Reliability – Our team is efficient, flexible, and agile only because we trust the reliability of each member. We need self-starters and goal-oriented individuals for our continued success.

• Curiosity – Continuous learning is a cornerstone at Doximity, and curious individuals thrive in our environment. We’re looking for someone who is curious enough about data to go above-and-beyond the task for the true insight.

• Respect – A key dynamic that allows our team to flourish is respect: for ourselves and our quality of work, for our teammates, and for our internal clients who are under the pressure of deadlines and finance goals.

About you:

• At least 4 years of professional experience as a Data Scientist or other related roles working with complex, high-volume, structured and unstructured datasets.

• Prior experience in a data science consulting role at firms such as ZS, Trinity, IQVIA, BlueMatter, etc., where you thrived in a fast-paced environment

• Advanced knowledge of statistical concepts — particularly exploratory data analysis, experimental design, and probability theory.

• Deep understanding of modern machine learning techniques

• Proven ability to design, train, and evaluate large-scale production models using frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.

• Advanced SQL proficiency — skilled at writing and optimizing complex queries across multiple tables and data relationships.

• Advanced Python skills, including understanding of object-oriented programming, production-grade code design, and modern data science libraries.

• Hands-on experience with distributed data processing tools and concepts for scalable analysis and model training.

• Excellent data visualization and storytelling abilities, with the capacity to translate technical insights into clear, compelling narratives for internal and client stakeholders.

• Curious, fast learner with a demonstrated passion for data, continuous learning, and staying current with advances in machine learning research.

Fun Facts About the Client Intelligence team

• We have access to one of the richest healthcare datasets in the world, with deep information on hundreds of thousands of clinicians and their connections.

• Business decisions at Doximity are driven by our data, analyses, and insights.

• The members of our team bring a diverse set of technical and cultural backgrounds.

• We like to have fun - company outings, team lunches, and other social events!

Compensation

The anticipated total compensation for this role is $119,333 - $172,800 depending on factors such as experience, skills, location, and internal equity.

Our total compensation package may include:

• Base salary

• Equity (where applicable)

• Annual bonus or incentive compensation (where applicable)

Specific compensation details will be discussed during the interview process.

Benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, Doximity offers a comprehensive benefits package for full time employees. Some of our offerings include:

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401(k) with company match

• Flexible paid time off and company holidays

• Paid parental leave

• Professional development and learning opportunities

• Wellness and mental health resources

• Remote work support and home office stipend (where applicable)

Why You'll Love Working Here

At Doximity, you'll join a mission-driven company where your work has a meaningful impact on healthcare. We believe great ideas come from empowered teams, and we're committed to creating an environment where people can do their best work.

• Make a real impact. Help build products that support over a million healthcare professionals and ultimately improve patient care.

• Work with exceptional teammates. Collaborate with thoughtful, talented colleagues who value curiosity, humility, and continuous learning.

• Enjoy flexibility and trust. We support flexible ways of working and empower employees with the autonomy to own their work.

• Grow your career. Take on meaningful challenges, develop new skills, and shape your career through mentorship and professional development.

• Bring your authentic self. We're committed to fostering an inclusive culture where diverse perspectives are welcomed, respected, and celebrated.

Our Hiring Process & AI Tools

Doximity may use artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools throughout the hiring process to help improve the candidate experience and support our recruiting team. These tools may assist with administrative tasks such as scheduling, general communication, interview coordination, note-taking, or summarizing interview feedback. Human recruiters and hiring managers make all hiring decisions. We are committed to using AI responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable laws.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Doximity is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know so we can support your participation.
